Longitudinal Summary

Over the periods from Q2 2021 through Q4 2025, the company consistently reported net income figures and detailed income tax expenses and benefits, with income tax rates fluctuating between benefits and expenses depending on the quarter and fiscal year. Operating income showed significant growth in later years, particularly in fiscal years 2024 and 2025, driven by higher revenues in key segments. Other income (expense), net primarily consisted of interest income and gains or losses from investments and foreign currency impacts, with occasional income reported. The company did not provide explicit forward guidance on income, focusing instead on reporting actual results and tax expense details in filings.

Forecasting Credibility: None

No guidance versus actual pairs were found for income, so it is not possible to assess management's forecasting credibility on this topic. The absence of forward guidance on income is common for accounting line items that are less subject to forecasting, such as net income or income tax expense. Therefore, no credibility rating can be assigned based on the available data.

Trends

  • Increasing operating income over time
  • Fluctuating income tax expense and benefits
  • Rising income tax expense as a percentage of income before tax in later years
  • Other income (expense), net generally small but occasionally positive
  • Net income reported consistently without forward guidance

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • Variability in income tax rates and benefits
  • Impact of investment gains/losses and foreign currency on other income
  • Dependence on revenue growth for operating income increases

Key Concerns

  • No forward guidance on income or net income limits ability to assess forecasting accuracy
  • Income tax expense as a percentage of income before tax shows variability that could affect net income predictability
  • No noted accounting or reporting inconsistencies, but reliance on filing-sourced actuals highlights importance of precise disclosures

Conclusion

Income has been reported consistently with detailed tax expense disclosures, showing growth in operating income driven by revenue increases. However, management does not provide forward guidance on income or net income, preventing an evaluation of forecasting credibility. Income tax expense fluctuates and can be a significant factor affecting net income, with benefits and expenses varying by period. Overall, while income figures are reliable as per filings, the lack of guidance means investors cannot rely on management forecasts for income, and must instead focus on reported results and tax expense trends.

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"As a multinational corporation, we are subject to income taxes as well as non-income-based taxes, such as payroll, sales, use, value-added, net worth, property and goods and services taxes, in both the United States and various foreign jurisdictions."
  • jump to section"Any changes in our effective tax rate may impact net income."
  • jump to section"Significant judgment is required in determining our worldwide provision for income taxes and other tax liabilities."
  • jump to section"Our future effective tax rate may also be affected by such factors as changes in our business or statutory rates, changes in jurisdictions in which our profits are determined to be earned and taxed, changes in available tax credits and deductions, the resolution of issues arising from tax audits, changes in United States generally accepted accounting principles, adjustments to income taxes upon finalization of tax returns, increases in expenses not deductible for tax purposes, changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities and in deferred tax valuation allowances, changing interpretation of existing laws or regulations, the impact of accounting for stock-based compensation and volatility in our stock price affecting the recognition of excess tax benefits and tax deficiencies within the income tax provision in the period in which they occur, the impact of accounting for business combinations, shifts in the amount of earnings in the United States compared with other regions in the world and overall levels of income before tax, changes in the domestic or international organization of our business and structure, as well as the expiration of statute of limitations and settlements of audits."
  • jump to section"Although we believe our tax estimates are reasonable, tax authorities may disagree with certain positions we have taken, and any adverse outcome of such a review or audit could increase our worldwide effective tax rate, increase the amount of non-income taxes imposed on our business, and harm our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows."
  • jump to section"Further, changes in United States federal, and state or international tax laws applicable to multinational corporations or other fundamental law changes, including changes to existing tax rules and regulations under the current U.S. administration and Congress, such as resulting from the recently enacted Inflation Reduction Act, parts of which are effective for us in fiscal year 2023, and as a result of recommendations from intergovernmental economic organizations such as the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, may materially impact our tax expense, the amount of non-income tax imposed on our business, and cash flows."

  • jump to section"As a multinational corporation, we are subject to income taxes as well as non-income-based taxes, such as payroll, sales, use, value-added, net worth, property and goods and services taxes, in both the United States and various foreign jurisdictions."

  • jump to section"Our future effective tax rate may also be affected by changes in our business or statutory rates, changes in jurisdictions in which our profits are determined to be earned and taxed, changes in available tax credits, the resolution of issues arising from tax audits, changes in United States generally accepted accounting principles, adjustments to income taxes upon finalization of tax returns, increases in expenses not deductible for tax purposes, changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities and in deferred tax valuation allowances, changing interpretation of existing laws or regulations, the impact of accounting for stock-based compensation and the recognition of excess tax benefits and tax deficiencies within the income tax provision in the period in which they occur, the impact of accounting for business combinations, shifts in the amount of earnings in the United States compared with other regions in the world and overall levels of income before tax, changes in the domestic or international organization of our business and structure, as well as the expiration of statute of limitations and settlements of audits."

  • jump to section"Most of our income is taxable in the United States, with a significant portion qualifying for preferential treatment as foreign-derived intangible income, or FDII."

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"Most of our income is taxable in the U.S., with a significant portion qualifying for preferential treatment as foreign-derived intangible income, or FDII."
  • jump to section"We are subject to complex income tax laws and regulations, as well as non-income-based taxes, in various jurisdictions."
  • jump to section"If U.S. tax rates increase or the FDII deduction is reduced, our provision for income taxes, results of operations, net income, and cash flows would be adversely affected."
  • jump to section"Significant judgment is required in determining our worldwide provision for income taxes and other tax liabilities."
  • jump to section"Any such tax laws, or changes in any such tax laws may increase tax uncertainty and compliance costs and adversely affect our provision for income taxes, cash tax payments, results of operations, and financial condition."
  • jump to section"Although we believe our tax estimates are reasonable, any adverse outcome could increase our worldwide effective tax rate, increase the amount of non-income taxes imposed on our business, and harm our financial position, results of operations, net income, and cash flows."
